Appearance:
 Shri Pankaj Thakkar - advocate for the appellant.
Shri Kshitij Vyas, learned Panel Lawyer for the State  ORDER 1.
Heard and perused the record.

2.This is an appeal filed by appellants under section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.451/2024,
registered at Police Station Kannod, District Dewas (MP) for offence under Sections 344, 376,
376(2)(n), 506 of IPC and under Sections 3(I)(W)(II), 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

3. This appeal under Section 14(A)(2) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against order dated 8.10.2024 passed by Special Judge [under SC/ST(PA) Act] District Dewas,
in Special Case / Bail Application No.1099/2024 whereby learned Special Judge rejected the bail application of appellants.
He is in detention since 02.07.2024.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3230 2 CRA-14200-2024 4.
Allegation against the appellant is that he has committed rape upon the prosecutrix.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the appellant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The prosecutrix resided with applicant from 20.4.2024 Ayat Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025

1 to 22.6.2024 i.e. more than two months.
FIR was lodged on 30.6.2024.
No missing report has been lodged.
As per the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, the relations are appearing consensual.
So far as the viral photos are concerned, since no photograph has been seized by the prosecution it is also not substantial.
He is in jail since 02.07.2024 and final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant/accused be released on bail, pending the trial.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer.

7. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case and custody period of the appellant, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant-accused is not warranted.

Consequently,
appeal stands allowed.

8. It is directed that appellant be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3230 3 CRA-14200-2024 by it during trial.

The appellant shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
